note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. claims.title: Roman conquest of Britain begins
claims.summary: The emperor Claudius launched the Roman invasion of Britain, beginning nearly four centuries of Roman rule over the province of Britannia, with its towns, roads, and the frontier of Hadrian's Wall.

sources.label: Story of England: 1066 and the Norman Conquest

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-43-roman-conquest-of-britain-begins, claim TL:GBR:event:43:roman-conquest-of-britain-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: End of Roman Britain
claims.summary: Roman authority was effectively withdrawn from Britain around 410, after which the former province fragmented and Germanic-speaking peoples gradually settled across what became England.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-410-end-of-roman-britain, claim TL:GBR:event:410:end-of-roman-britain, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Alfred defeats the Vikings at Edington
claims.summary: Alfred the Great of Wessex won a decisive victory over the Viking 'Great Heathen Army' at Edington, securing the survival of Anglo-Saxon rule in southern England and beginning the path to unification.

sources.label: The British Library: history and collections

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-878-alfred-defeats-the-vikings-at-edington, claim TL:GBR:event:878:alfred-defeats-the-vikings-at-edington, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: England unified under Athelstan
claims.summary: By capturing Viking-held York and securing the submission of other rulers, Athelstan became the first king to rule over all of England, forging a single English kingdom.

sources.label: Room 41: Sutton Hoo and Europe — Large Print Guide
Story of England: 1066 and the Norman Conquest

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-927-england-unified-under-athelstan, claim TL:GBR:event:927:england-unified-under-athelstan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Hastings and the Norman Conquest
claims.summary: William of Normandy defeated and killed King Harold II at Hastings and was crowned king on Christmas Day, beginning Norman rule and transforming England's language, law, and aristocracy.

sources.label: Story of England: 1066 and the Norman Conquest

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1066-battle-of-hastings-and-the-norman-conquest, claim TL:GBR:event:1066:battle-of-hastings-and-the-norman-conquest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Domesday Book compiled
claims.summary: William the Conqueror ordered a comprehensive survey of landholding in England, producing Domesday Book, an unparalleled record of the kingdom's wealth and the new Norman order.

sources.label: The British Library: history and collections

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1086-domesday-book-compiled, claim TL:GBR:event:1086:domesday-book-compiled, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Magna Carta sealed at Runnymede
claims.summary: Rebel barons compelled King John to seal Magna Carta, asserting that the monarch was bound by law; though soon annulled, it became a lasting symbol of limits on royal power.

sources.label: The British Library: history and collections

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1215-magna-carta-sealed-at-runnymede, claim TL:GBR:event:1215:magna-carta-sealed-at-runnymede, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Black Death reaches England
claims.summary: The plague pandemic killed a large proportion of England's population within a few years, devastating communities and accelerating long-term changes in labour and society.

sources.label: The British Library: history and collections

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1348-the-black-death-reaches-england, claim TL:GBR:event:1348:the-black-death-reaches-england, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Bosworth ends the Wars of the Roses
claims.summary: Henry Tudor defeated Richard III at Bosworth Field, ending the Plantagenet dynasty and the Wars of the Roses and founding the Tudor line as Henry VII.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1485-battle-of-bosworth-ends-the-wars-of-the-roses, claim TL:GBR:event:1485:battle-of-bosworth-ends-the-wars-of-the-roses, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Act of Supremacy and the break with Rome
claims.summary: Parliament declared Henry VIII Supreme Head of the Church of England, ending papal authority in England and launching the English Reformation and the dissolution of the monasteries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1534-act-of-supremacy-and-the-break-with-rome, claim TL:GBR:event:1534:act-of-supremacy-and-the-break-with-rome, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Laws in Wales Acts incorporate Wales into England
claims.summary: Two Acts of Henry VIII's Parliament (27 Hen. 8 c. 26, cited as 1535, and 34 & 35 Hen. 8 c. 26 of 1542) declared Wales incorporated with England, extended English law and administration to it, and divided it into twelve shires. The 1535 Act was repealed on 21 December 1993.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1536-the-laws-in-wales-acts-incorporate-wales-into, claim TL:GBR:event:1536:the-laws-in-wales-acts-incorporate-wales-into, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Elizabethan Religious Settlement
claims.summary: Elizabeth I's settlement re-established royal headship of the Church and a Protestant order, ending decades of religious upheaval and shaping the Church of England for centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1559-the-elizabethan-religious-settlement, claim TL:GBR:event:1559:the-elizabethan-religious-settlement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Defeat of the Spanish Armada
claims.summary: England repelled the Spanish Armada sent by Philip II, a decisive check to Spanish ambitions that bolstered English naval confidence and national identity.

sources.label: God blew and they were scattered

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1588-defeat-of-the-spanish-armada, claim TL:GBR:event:1588:defeat-of-the-spanish-armada, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the East India Company
claims.summary: A royal charter created the East India Company for trade with Asia; over the following centuries it grew into an instrument of conquest that brought much of India under British control.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1600-founding-of-the-east-india-company, claim TL:GBR:event:1600:founding-of-the-east-india-company, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Union of the Crowns
claims.summary: James VI of Scotland succeeded Elizabeth I as James I of England, uniting the English and Scottish crowns under one monarch while the two kingdoms remained separate states.

sources.label: The British Library: history and collections

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1603-union-of-the-crowns, claim TL:GBR:event:1603:union-of-the-crowns, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Execution of Charles I
claims.summary: After defeat in the English Civil War, Charles I was tried and beheaded, and a republican Commonwealth was established — a singular assertion of Parliament's power over the crown.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1649-execution-of-charles-i, claim TL:GBR:event:1649:execution-of-charles-i, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Glorious Revolution
claims.summary: James II was deposed and William and Mary took the throne on Parliament's terms; the Bill of Rights of 1689 entrenched parliamentary authority and constitutional monarchy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1688-the-glorious-revolution, claim TL:GBR:event:1688:the-glorious-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Acts of Union create Great Britain
claims.summary: The Acts of Union merged the kingdoms and parliaments of England and Scotland into a single Kingdom of Great Britain, governed by one Parliament at Westminster.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1707-acts-of-union-create-great-britain, claim TL:GBR:event:1707:acts-of-union-create-great-britain, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Loss of the American colonies
claims.summary: The Treaty of Paris recognised the independence of the United States, ending the American Revolutionary War and stripping Britain of its thirteen mainland colonies.

sources.label: The British Library: history and collections

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1783-loss-of-the-american-colonies, claim TL:GBR:event:1783:loss-of-the-american-colonies, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Union with Ireland forms the United Kingdom
claims.summary: The Acts of Union 1800 merged the kingdoms of Great Britain and Ireland, creating the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland and abolishing the separate Irish parliament.

sources.label: Act for the Union of Great Britain and Ireland

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1801-union-with-ireland-forms-the-united-kingdom, claim TL:GBR:event:1801:union-with-ireland-forms-the-united-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Abolition of the British slave trade
claims.summary: The Slave Trade Act prohibited the Atlantic slave trade across the British Empire, though it did not free those already enslaved in British colonies.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1807-abolition-of-the-british-slave-trade, claim TL:GBR:event:1807:abolition-of-the-british-slave-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Slavery Abolition Act
claims.summary: Parliament abolished slavery across most of the British Empire, effective 1834, freeing more than 800,000 people while compensating former slave-owners rather than the enslaved.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1833-slavery-abolition-act, claim TL:GBR:event:1833:slavery-abolition-act, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Great Irish Famine
claims.summary: Potato blight and an inadequate, laissez-faire government response caused mass starvation in Ireland, killing roughly a million people and forcing about a million more to emigrate.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1845-the-great-irish-famine, claim TL:GBR:event:1845:the-great-irish-famine, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Victorian era and the height of empire
claims.summary: During Queen Victoria's long reign Britain became the world's foremost industrial and imperial power, its empire eventually spanning about a quarter of the globe.

sources.label: Victoria, Queen of the United Kingdom

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1837-the-victorian-era-and-the-height-of-empire, claim TL:GBR:event:1837:the-victorian-era-and-the-height-of-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The First World War
claims.summary: Britain and its empire fought in the First World War at enormous human cost; the war accelerated social and political change, including votes for women, and led to the partition of Ireland and the Irish Free State in 1922.

sources.label: The end of the British Empire after the Second World War

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1914-the-first-world-war, claim TL:GBR:event:1914:the-first-world-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Northern Ireland's Parliament opens
claims.summary: Under the Government of Ireland Act 1920, which defined Northern Ireland as the six counties of Antrim, Armagh, Down, Fermanagh, Londonderry and Tyrone, George V opened the Parliament of Northern Ireland in Belfast City Hall; unionists had won 40 of its 52 seats.

sources.label: 'Who is for the Empire and who is for the Republic?': the 1921 elections to the Northern Ireland parliament

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1921-northern-ireland-s-parliament-opens, claim TL:GBR:event:1921:northern-ireland-s-parliament-opens, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Royal and Parliamentary Titles Act renames the state
claims.summary: The Act changed the style of Parliament to 'of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland' and let the Crown alter its royal style; the proclamation followed on 13 May 1927.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1927-the-royal-and-parliamentary-titles-act-renames, claim TL:GBR:event:1927:the-royal-and-parliamentary-titles-act-renames, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Second World War
claims.summary: Britain fought Nazi Germany and the Axis, endured the Blitz, and emerged victorious but economically drained; the wartime Bengal famine of 1943 killed millions in British India.

sources.label: The end of the British Empire after the Second World War

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1939-the-second-world-war, claim TL:GBR:event:1939:the-second-world-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the National Health Service
claims.summary: The post-war Labour government launched the NHS, providing healthcare free at the point of use and forming the centrepiece of Britain's new welfare state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1948-founding-of-the-national-health-service, claim TL:GBR:event:1948:founding-of-the-national-health-service, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence of India and the start of decolonisation
claims.summary: India and Pakistan became independent, beginning the rapid dismantling of the British Empire as dozens of colonies gained independence over the following decades.

sources.label: The end of the British Empire after the Second World War

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1947-independence-of-india-and-the-start-of, claim TL:GBR:event:1947:independence-of-india-and-the-start-of, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ireland Act affirms Northern Ireland's status
claims.summary: Recognising that Éire had ceased to be part of His Majesty's dominions on 18 April 1949, the Ireland Act affirmed that Northern Ireland would not cease to be part of the United Kingdom without the consent of the Parliament of Northern Ireland.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1949-ireland-act-affirms-northern-ireland-s-status, claim TL:GBR:event:1949:ireland-act-affirms-northern-ireland-s-status, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Gibraltar votes to stay British
claims.summary: In a sovereignty referendum Gibraltarians chose to keep their link with Britain rather than pass under Spanish sovereignty, by 12,138 votes to 44; Spain responded by closing the land frontier in 1969.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1967-gibraltar-votes-to-stay-british, claim TL:GBR:event:1967:gibraltar-votes-to-stay-british, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Troubles in Northern Ireland
claims.summary: Three decades of conflict over Northern Ireland's constitutional status followed the civil rights protests of 1968. The Sutton Index records 3,532 deaths between July 1969 and 2001: 58 per cent caused by republican paramilitaries, 29 per cent by loyalist paramilitaries and 10 per cent by the British security forces.

sources.label: Sutton Index of Deaths: summary by organisation responsible
Malcolm Sutton: An Index of Deaths from the Conflict in Ireland

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1969-the-troubles-in-northern-ireland, claim TL:GBR:event:1969:the-troubles-in-northern-ireland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Internment without trial
claims.summary: Internment was introduced in Northern Ireland and used at first only against republicans; of 1,981 people detained before it ended in December 1975, 1,874 were Catholic or republican and 107 Protestant or loyalist. In Ballymurphy over the following days ten civilians were shot dead, nine of them by the Army, whom a 2021 inquest found 'entirely innocent'.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1971-internment-without-trial, claim TL:GBR:event:1971:internment-without-trial, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Direct rule from Westminster
claims.summary: Edward Heath's government prorogued the Stormont Parliament and imposed direct rule on Northern Ireland from Westminster.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1972-direct-rule-from-westminster, claim TL:GBR:event:1972:direct-rule-from-westminster, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Belfast (Good Friday) Agreement
claims.summary: The British and Irish governments and Northern Ireland parties agreed power-sharing and the principle of consent, given effect by the Northern Ireland Act 1998: Northern Ireland remains in the UK unless a majority of its people vote otherwise in a poll. Referendums on 22 May 1998 approved it by 71.1 per cent in Northern Ireland and 94.4 per cent in the Republic of Ireland.

sources.label: The 1998 Referendums
sources.publisher: ARK, Queen's University Belfast and Ulster University

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-1998-the-belfast-good-friday-agreement, claim TL:GBR:event:1998:the-belfast-good-friday-agreement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Gibraltar rejects shared sovereignty
claims.summary: In a referendum called by the Gibraltar Government, voters rejected a proposal for British–Spanish joint sovereignty by 17,900 votes to 187.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-2002-gibraltar-rejects-shared-sovereignty, claim TL:GBR:event:2002:gibraltar-rejects-shared-sovereignty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: De Silva review of the Finucane murder
claims.summary: A government-commissioned review of the 1989 killing of the Belfast solicitor Pat Finucane by the loyalist UDA found 'frankly shocking levels of state collusion' though no 'over-arching State conspiracy'; the Prime Minister apologised to his family.

sources.label: Prime Minister David Cameron statement on Patrick Finucane

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-2012-de-silva-review-of-the-finucane-murder, claim TL:GBR:event:2012:de-silva-review-of-the-finucane-murder, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The United Kingdom leaves the European Union
claims.summary: Following the 2016 referendum, the UK formally withdrew from the European Union, ending nearly half a century of membership in the European project.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of United Kingdom: From Roman province and warring kingdoms to a united realm, a global empire, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/GBR/chronicle#ev-2020-the-united-kingdom-leaves-the-european-union, claim TL:GBR:event:2020:the-united-kingdom-leaves-the-european-union, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Windsor Framework
claims.summary: Northern Ireland, which voted 55.8 per cent to remain in the 2016 referendum, was kept aligned with EU goods rules after Brexit; the UK and EU's Windsor Framework added a 'green lane' for goods staying in the UK and a 'Stormont brake' requiring 30 Assembly members from at least two parties.

sources.label: Windsor Framework unveiled to fix problems of the Northern Ireland Protocol
EU Referendum 2016 (Northern Ireland)
sources.publisher: ARK, Queen's University Belfast and Ulster University
